note: Fits the profile half and fails the commercial and starting-point tests. He runs an online and digital marketing business with his wife and previously distributed for Enagic, which places him inside 'business owner or equivalent', and he spent four years living in Cabo San Lucas. He is about as far from deconditioned as the corpus gets — minor professional hockey, close to the NHL, training since fifteen — and the goal is unambiguously good to great: core strength, body mechanics and keeping up with his kids into later life, not rescue. Income is a miss on the observed evidence: his reference price for a training programme is about $20 a month, he declined at CAD 270 a month, and he closed on 'obviously want to be mindful of money I spend.' Neglected health is a clear miss in the same direction as several others in this batch — he loves training, gets himself to the gym unaided, and has spent the last six months deliberately working on body mechanics. Health is the part of his life he is already tending; what he lacks is a plan, which is why he wanted a $20 product and not a $6,000 one.
